newsitem.title: PERU: Lima shrs gain strongly as investors re-enter mkt.
newsitem.headline: Lima shrs gain strongly as investors re-enter mkt.

text.p: Shares on the Lima stock exchange made strong gains Wednesday as investors were keen to buy Peruvian equities after Tuesday's news that the U.S. Federal Reserve would leave rates unchanged, brokers said.

The Fed's announcement came too late during the Lima session to have a large effect on Tuesday's trading. But Wednesday, investors, who had been sidelined awaiting the rates news, flooded back into the market, brokers said.
Thursday, prices were expected to climb less sharply than Wednesday as the effect of the Fed news was seen dying away, they added.
Wednesday, the General Index rose 2.20 percent to 1,588.6 points, while the blue-chip Selective Index climbed 1.91 percent to 2,119.0 points, according to preliminary stock figures.
In a total of 2,516 operations, 50 stocks rose, 24 fell and 34 were stable. Volume was an improved 38.0 million ($15.1 million).

"The market saw strong movement due to an influx of foreign capital, a visible increase in the number of locals investing and because of positive rumors for some companies," said Guillermo Siles of the local brokerage Argos.
Market rumors of an imminent fusion of the breweries Backus y Johnston and Compania Nacional de Cerveza gave impetus to the sector, which saw the day's biggest gains, brokers said.

Backus y Johnston rose 3.64 percent to 2.85 soles, accounting for ten percent of total volume, while Compania Nacional de Cerveza jumped 10.40 percent to 1.38 soles, representing nine percent of total trade.
The funds needed to buy heavily into brewery stocks distracted investment away from some other blue-chips, brokers said.
Benchmark Telefonica del Peru saw modest gains, climbing 0.36 percent to 5.61 soles, in volume accounting for 17 percent of the day's total trade.
Telecom Tele 2000 fared worse, dropping 1.19 percent to 4.15 soles in meager volume of 9,300 shares.
